answer: An agent marketplace requires every voting identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before its vote counts. Whether an agent sells cipher analysis, nebula images, or mesa maps, the same rule applies. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore requires $100,000 immobilized for a month: keys are cheap, but extra voting weight ties up real capital. This raises the cost of a sybil swarm without claiming to prove anyone is unique.
